title: 945, and Why Kernel decide Fails Here
content: **Framing.** A number is *abundant* when its proper divisors sum to more than itself. The smallest abundant number is 12, but it is *even*; every abundant number below 945 is even, and the smallest *odd* abundant number is $945 = 3^3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$, whose proper divisors sum to $975 > 945$ (OEIS A005231). The mathematical claim is a bounded finite check, but a naive `decide` on `Nat.Abundant` over the full 945-range forces the kernel to reduce `Finset.filter`/`Finset.sum` over `Finset.range n` — a `Quotient`-backed computation that exhausts the native reduction stack (build aborts with signal 135) under the pinned Lean/Mathlib v4.26 toolchain. The engineering fix is a kernel-friendly reformulation, delegated to `native_decide`.
relatedConcepts: Abundant numbers and the divisor-sum function σ
prerequisites: Quotient-backed Finset reduction and its cost in the kernel

title: pdSum: a Compiler-Evaluable Proper-Divisor Sum
content: **The kernel-friendly computation.** `pdSum n := ((List.range n).filter (fun d => decide (d ∣ n))).sum`. Instead of Mathlib's `Quotient`-backed `∑ d ∈ n.properDivisors, d`, this sums the divisors $d < n$ over a plain `List.range n` by structural recursion, using GMP-accelerated `Nat.mod` for the divisibility tests. This is the representation the two `native_decide` computations actually run on — the compiler evaluates it quickly where the kernel's Finset reduction would stall.
mathContext: $\mathtt{pdSum}\,n = \sum_{d < n,\ d \mid n} d$ — the same value as the proper-divisor sum, but computed without any `Quotient`.

title: The Symbolic Bridge to properDivisors
content: **Correctness, proved off the decide path.** `listRange_filter_sum_eq`: $((\mathrm{List.range}\,n).\mathrm{filter}\,(p\,\cdot)).\mathrm{sum} = \sum_{i \in (\mathrm{Finset.range}\,n).\mathrm{filter}\,p} i$, proved by induction — `List.range_succ` + `List.filter_append` on the List side against `Finset.range_succ` + `Finset.filter_insert` on the Finset side, with a `by_cases` on $p\,k$. Being an induction, it is robust to exact Mathlib lemma names. `pdSum_eq` then specialises it: $\mathtt{pdSum}\,n = \sum_{d \in n.\mathrm{properDivisors}} d$ for $n \ne 0$, via `Nat.filter_dvd_eq_properDivisors`. Both are ordinary kernel proofs, invoked *symbolically* — never under `decide` — so the fast List representation carries a proof of correctness against Mathlib's `Nat.Abundant`.
mathContext: The bridge is proved *once* and kernel-checked; the expensive finite enumeration then runs on `pdSum` while abundance is stated in terms of Mathlib's proper-divisor sum.
relatedConcepts: Induction bridging a List sum to a Finset sum
Separating fast computation from symbolic correctness

title: The Two native_decide Computations (Lean.ofReduceBool)
content: **Where the axiom enters.** `abundant_945`: `Nat.Abundant 945`, unfolded and rewritten through `pdSum_eq` to $945 < \mathtt{pdSum}\,945$, closed by `native_decide` (line 73). `check_odd_below`: $\forall n < 945,\ \mathrm{Odd}\,n \to \mathtt{pdSum}\,n \le n$, closed by `native_decide` (line 82), with the `Odd n` hypothesis evaluated first so the ~472 even cases short-circuit without computing `pdSum`. `odd_945` ($\mathrm{Odd}\,945$) is by ordinary kernel `decide`. These two `native_decide` calls trust the compiler's reduction and so introduce the `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom — the reason the entry is **axiomatized** ($\mathtt{meta.axiomCount} = 1$), even though there are 0 literal `axiom` declarations ($\mathtt{leanFile.axiomCount} = 0$).
mathContext: `native_decide` compiles the decidable Boolean and certifies its value via `Lean.ofReduceBool`; the ordinary foundational axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound are not counted, but `Lean.ofReduceBool` is.
relatedConcepts: Short-circuiting even cases via the Odd hypothesis
Axiom Integrity Policy: axiomatized vs. verified
prerequisites: The meaning of the Lean.ofReduceBool axiom

title: Assembling Minimality: IsLeast at 945
content: **The headline.** `not_abundant_odd_below`: no odd $n < 945$ is abundant — transports `check_odd_below` back to `Nat.Abundant` through `pdSum_eq` and `Nat.not_lt`. `smallest_odd_abundant`: $\mathrm{IsLeast}\,\{n : \mathrm{Odd}\,n \wedge \mathrm{Nat.Abundant}\,n\}\,945$ — the membership half is `⟨odd_945, abundant_945⟩`, and the lower-bound half assumes an odd abundant $n$, `by_contra`/`push_neg` puts it below 945, and `not_abundant_odd_below` yields the contradiction. This packages the kernel-checked scaffolding and the two compiler-checked leaves into the final extremal statement.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsLeast}\,S\,945$ means $945 \in S$ and $945 \in \mathrm{lowerBounds}\,S$: 945 is odd and abundant, and dominates every odd abundant number from below.
relatedConcepts: Transporting a pdSum bound back to Nat.Abundant
